features.description: S3 bucket operations with HIPAA auto-config
steps: src/lib/s3-buckets.ts: createHipaaBucket() orchestrates CreateBucket → PutBucketOwnershipControls (BucketOwnerEnforced, disables ACLs to close the pre-PAB window — sec-review H1) → PutPublicAccessBlock (all 4 flags) → PutBucketVersioning (Enabled) → PutBucketEncryption (SSE-KMS with CMK + BucketKeyEnabled=true) → PutBucketLogging (to AWS_S3_LOGS_BUCKET with s3-access-logs/<bucket>/ prefix) → PutBucketPolicy (DenyNonHttps via aws:SecureTransport=false)

Best-effort rollback (sec-review H2): try/catch after CreateBucket attempts DeleteBucket on any post-create failure; if rollback DeleteBucket itself fails, console.warn with explicit 'rollback FAILED / manual remediation required' so the bucket cannot silently exist half-configured
Bucket name validation: 3–63 chars lowercase alphanumeric + hyphens, no leading/trailing hyphen, no underscores/dots; reject AWS-reserved 'xn--' prefix and '-s3alias' suffix (sec-review H1 sub-item)
BucketLocationConstraint used for region cast (code-review HIGH — replaces unsafe 'us-west-2' literal cast); us-east-1 still sent WITHOUT CreateBucketConfiguration per S3 quirk

CloudTrail data events via read-modify-write (sec-review C1 CRITICAL fix): GetEventSelectorsCommand → mergeBucketIntoSelectors() (immutable — returns new array, original untouched) → PutEventSelectorsCommand. Previous naive PutEventSelectors would have wiped every previously-registered bucket on second createHipaaBucket call. Idempotent: re-registering same bucket does not duplicate its ARN

src/lib/cloudtrail.ts new singleton mirroring s3.ts pattern: getCloudTrailClient() with explicit AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID + AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY credentials from validated config (code-review HIGH — previous inline `new CloudTrailClient({ region })` used implicit provider chain divergent from S3 client)

config.ts: added AWS_CLOUDTRAIL_NAME optional env with empty-string-to-undefined transform. When unset, createHipaaBucket still applies every S3 control but returns cloudTrailConfigured=false carry-forward flag so the deploy runbook surfaces the gap before go-live
httpsOnlyBucketPolicy(bucket) returns JSON string with Principal:* Action:s3:* (locks out account root too when non-HTTPS — intentional HIPAA behaviour, document in runbook)
listHipaaBuckets() returns normalized [{Name, CreationDate}] via ListBucketsCommand (carry-forward: filter to managed buckets by DB join in F5.1 — currently returns entire AWS account bucket list)

deleteEmptyHipaaBucket(name): validates name, ListObjectsV2 MaxKeys=1 preflight (throws BucketNotEmptyError if KeyCount>0), DeleteBucketCommand; TOCTOU-safe rewrap: AWS BucketNotEmpty/BucketNotEmptyException rethrow as BucketNotEmptyError so callers see a single error surface
InvalidBucketNameError + BucketNotEmptyError custom classes for typed error handling (following ConfigError pattern)

Test mock strategy: vi.doMock('@/lib/s3') + vi.doMock('@/lib/cloudtrail') to inject fake send() spies; no live AWS calls. 25 tests covering LocationConstraint regional branch, all 6 S3 commands, ordering assertions, 5 invalid-name variants + xn-- / -s3alias reserved-name guards, rollback-on-failure (3 scenarios: mid-setup failure, failed rollback-warn, no-rollback-on-create-failure), CloudTrail read-modify-write, CloudTrail idempotency, CloudTrail missing-trail carry-forward, CloudTrail error propagation, mergeBucketIntoSelectors immutability unit tests, listHipaaBuckets normalization, deleteEmptyHipaaBucket TOCTOU rewrap

Carry-forward (deploy runbook): (a) logs bucket existence + S3 LogDelivery group ACL grants — sec-review M2; (b) HTTPS-only policy locks out root account for non-HTTPS ops; (c) DB-scoped bucket filter in F5.1 listing; (d) account-level Block Public Access assertion at deploy time
src/lib/s3-presign.ts: presignPutUrl (upload) + presignGetUrl (download) via @aws-sdk/s3-request-presigner getSignedUrl

Split TTL caps by verb (sec-review MEDIUM): MIN_TTL_SECONDS=900 (15 min) floor for both; MAX_PUT_TTL_SECONDS=3600 (1 hour) for writes — stolen upload URL overwrite window tight; MAX_GET_TTL_SECONDS=604800 (7 days) matches SigV4 protocol cap for reads (F9 link engine layers policy + revocation + download-count gating on top). MAX_TTL_SECONDS retained as alias for backward compat. DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS=900 for both

presignPutUrl bakes SSE-KMS params via withSseKms (code-review HIGH fix — was inlining ServerSideEncryption/SSEKMSKeyId/BucketKeyEnabled directly; now reuses src/lib/s3.ts helper so a future KMS-key-rotation change propagates). Upload client MUST send matching x-amz-server-side-encryption* headers or S3 returns 403 — unencrypted uploads impossible
ContentType on PUT is hoisted into the signed URL via signableHeaders: new Set(['content-type']) — uploader cannot swap MIME type post-signature (MIME confusion guard)

Input validation at boundary: assertTargets rejects empty bucket + empty key, keys starting with '/', and keys containing '..' segments (sec-review MEDIUM). assertTtl enforces Number.isFinite (NaN/Infinity/negative blocked) + per-verb bound. assertContentType uses RFC 6838 subset regex. assertContentDisposition allows only 'attachment' | 'inline' with optional quoted safe-char filename (sec-review HIGH — blocks XSS-via-MIME-override and filename-injection attacks on GET response overrides)

presignGetUrl supports ResponseContentDisposition + ResponseContentType for download filename/type override — both validated. ResponseContentDisposition is SDK-serialized as query parameter not header, so no signableHeaders needed
Typed errors: InvalidPresignTtlError, InvalidPresignTargetError, InvalidResponseOverrideError — consistent with ConfigError/InvalidBucketNameError sibling pattern
Bearer-token reality documented in JSDoc on presignPutUrl: never log the URL, keep TTL as short as UX tolerates, S3 lacks native one-time-use semantics

18 tests: happy-path URL structure (PUT + GET), SSE-KMS signed-headers, default + explicit TTL propagation, per-verb TTL rejection (PUT 3601 vs GET 604801), NaN/Infinity/negative TTL rejection, empty bucket/key rejection, key traversal + leading-slash rejection, malformed contentType rejection (MIME confusion), ResponseContentDisposition happy path, ResponseContentDisposition injection rejection (backslash-quote, filename traversal, no action token), ResponseContentType MIME override rejection, all exported TTL constants

src/lib/s3-objects.ts: listObjects (ListObjectsV2) with configurable delimiter (default '/' for folder view, empty string for flat recursive — code-review MEDIUM fix to avoid F6 listing regressions), prefix + continuation pagination, maxKeys clamp [1..1000], normalized result shape (contents/commonPrefixes/nextContinuationToken/isTruncated)

listObjectVersions (ListObjectVersions) exposing Versions + DeleteMarkers merged into a single [{key,versionId,isLatest,isDeleteMarker,size,lastModified}] array — added for F6.5 superadmin hard-delete UX (code-review LOW fix — avoids future API route reaching past the facade)

headObject returns ObjectMetadata with allowlisted userMetadata (sec-review MEDIUM fix — ALLOWED_USER_METADATA_KEYS = {uploader, filename, tenant-id, content-type} drops every other x-amz-meta-* key as defense-in-depth against PHI leaking through the read path even if upload route validator fails)

copyObject: URL-encodes CopySource per-segment (preserves '/' separators, encodes spaces + non-ASCII), MetadataDirective: 'COPY' + sseKmsParams() — confirmed orthogonal per AWS docs, re-encrypts destination with OUR CMK regardless of source encryption

moveObject = copyObject then DeleteObject on source; copy failure leaves source untouched. If process crashes between copy and delete, both objects exist — accepted degraded state (no data loss, ops reconciles via versioning) documented in code comment

softDeleteObject vs hardDeleteObjectVersion split (sec-review MEDIUM fix — previously single deleteObject accepted optional versionId; footgun risk of accidental hard-delete from lower-privilege route). softDeleteObject omits VersionId (places delete marker). hardDeleteObjectVersion requires non-empty versionId (validated), named explicitly to signal superadmin-only intent so accidental import is impossible

deleteObjects bulk: input key validation, 1000-key batch cap (S3 API limit), Promise.all parallelization across batches (code-review HIGH fix — was sequential; 2500 keys now 1 round-trip instead of 3). Aggregates Deleted + Errors across all batches

Key validation (assertKey) rejects: empty, '..' segments, '/' leading, trailing, or consecutive (empty-segment guard — code-review MEDIUM fix for encodeCopySource edge case with folder-marker keys like 'folder/')
InvalidObjectTargetError custom class with {bucket|key|prefix|keys} target union for consistent error surface

19 tests: listObjects folder + flat + prefix/continuation + maxKeys clamp + invalid-prefix, listObjectVersions merge + pagination, headObject allowlist filter (verifies phi-ssn + unauthorized-key dropped) + 5 invalid-key variants, copyObject URL encoding + SSE-KMS on dest + invalid-target rejection (empty / traversal / empty-segment), moveObject ordering + no-delete-on-copy-failure, softDeleteObject + hardDeleteObjectVersion separation + versionId requirement, deleteObjects 3-key batch + 2500-key parallel batching + Deleted/Errors aggregation + empty-array + traversal rejection

features.description: Multipart upload support for large files
steps: src/lib/s3-multipart.ts: initiateMultipartUpload / presignUploadPart / completeMultipartUpload / abortMultipartUpload + helpers shouldUseMultipart, assertFileSize, planMultipartParts

Constants: MULTIPART_THRESHOLD_BYTES=100MB (strict >, documented in shouldUseMultipart JSDoc), MAX_FILE_SIZE_BYTES=5GB, MIN_PART_SIZE_BYTES=5MB (S3 hard minimum except last), MAX_PART_NUMBER=10000, TARGET_PART_SIZE_BYTES=10MB

initiateMultipartUpload bakes sseKmsParams() into CreateMultipartUploadCommand — UploadPart inherits encryption context from the init session so a stolen part presigned URL cannot write unencrypted bytes

declaredSizeBytes optional input on initiate (sec-review HIGH fix): when supplied, assertFileSize runs BEFORE the UploadId is issued, so the 5 GB HIPAA cap is enforced server-side even if the API route forgets to validate the client-declared size separately
presignUploadPart: TTL clamped to s3-presign's MAX_PUT_TTL_SECONDS (1 hour) and MIN_TTL_SECONDS (15 min); partNumber validated to [1, 10000] integer

completeMultipartUpload: ETag format validation via /^"[0-9a-fA-F]{32}(?:-\d+)?"$/ per part (sec-review MEDIUM fix — blocks obviously-fabricated client ETags before S3 round-trip), contiguous 1..N PartNumber sequence check (sec-review MEDIUM fix — rejects gaps like [1,2,5] client-side before InvalidPartOrder from S3), duplicate PartNumber check, non-mutating sort via [...input.parts].sort(), ETag returned as non-optional string in CompleteMultipartResult (code-review LOW — F6.2 can statically rely on it for DB persistence)

abortMultipartUpload releases uploaded parts' storage. Comment documents the deploy-runbook carry-forward (sec-review MEDIUM M3): every document bucket must have an AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload lifecycle rule (1–7 day window) as the safety net when this function is never reached due to client abandonment

assertKey aligned with s3-presign + s3-objects siblings (sec-review MEDIUM fix + code-review HIGH): rejects empty, leading '/', '..' segments, empty path segments — prevents API routes from smuggling bad keys past one validator by routing through a different module

Shared assertContentType exported from s3-presign.ts (code-review HIGH fix) — InvalidResponseOverrideError reused for contentType errors across upload surface; InvalidPresignTargetError reused for bucket/key; InvalidMultipartInputError retained only for multipart-specific fields (uploadId, partNumber, parts, size)

planMultipartParts: dynamic floor = max(10MB target, ceil(size/10000), 5MB S3 minimum) — documented in code (code-review MEDIUM fix — previous Math.max was dead code; now the clamp is future-proof if MAX_FILE_SIZE_BYTES grows beyond 100GB)

22 tests: constants export, initiate (SSE-KMS baked, optional contentType omitted path, no UploadId error, declaredSize cap gate, leading-slash rejection, empty/traversal/empty-segment key rejection, malformed contentType), presignUploadPart (URL structure, partNumber bounds + NaN, empty uploadId, TTL cap), complete (sorted parts + return fields, empty array, duplicate PartNumber, malformed ETag, non-contiguous PartNumber sequence), abort (happy + empty uploadId), size helpers (shouldUseMultipart strict-greater semantics, assertFileSize bounds, planMultipartParts exact-multiple + non-multiple-with-remainder)

src/lib/iam-policies.ts: policy documents as runtime TypeScript exports (so tests validate AND deploy tooling can emit verbatim — prevents doc drift). Exports buildAppRolePolicy, buildHipaaBucketPolicy, buildDocumentKmsKeyPolicy, plus BUCKET_ARN_PATTERN / BUCKET_OBJECTS_ARN_PATTERN constants
IamStatement interface includes optional Principal field (code-review MEDIUM fix — required for resource-based policies: bucket + KMS key policies)
App role policy (buildAppRolePolicy):
Allow — S3ObjectReadWrite scoped to helpucompli-docs-*/*

Allow — S3BucketReadAndHipaaProvisioning scoped to helpucompli-docs-* (CreateBucket, DeleteBucket, Put/GetBucketVersioning, Put/GetBucketEncryption, Put/GetBucketLogging, Put/GetPublicAccessBlock, Put/GetBucketOwnershipControls, Put/GetBucketPolicy) — runtime role needs these for F5.2 superadmin flow + F3.2 createHipaaBucket; bounded by app-layer auth + Zod validation + compensating Denies
Allow — S3ListAllMyBucketsForAdminUI with Resource:* (AWS only accepts *; F5.1 DB join filters to managed buckets)
Allow — KmsDocumentCmkUsage (kms:Decrypt, GenerateDataKey, DescribeKey) scoped to AWS_KMS_KEY_ID ARN
Allow — CloudTrailDataEventWiring (GetEventSelectors, PutEventSelectors) scoped to configured trail ARN

Deny — DenyLoggingBucketMutation (sec-review HIGH fix — s3:PutBucketLogging, DeleteBucketLogging on the access-logs bucket itself; previously runtime could silently redirect audit trail since helpucompli-docs-access-logs matched the helpucompli-docs-* Allow pattern)
Deny — DenyBucketAclMutation (s3:PutBucketAcl + PutObjectAcl defense-in-depth on top of BucketOwnerEnforced)
Deny — DenyKmsLifecycle (kms:CreateKey, ScheduleKeyDeletion, CancelKeyDeletion, DisableKey, PutKeyPolicy, CreateGrant, RevokeGrant)

Deny — DenyIamAndCloudTrailAdmin narrowed to IAM write surface (sec-review MEDIUM fix — iam:Create*/Delete*/Attach*/Detach*/Put*/Update*/PassRole instead of blanket iam:* which would have blocked implicit iam:GetRole/ListRoles reads from SDK)

Bucket policy (buildHipaaBucketPolicy): DenyNonHttps with explicit Principal:* (code-review MEDIUM fix — was implicit in runtime s3-buckets.ts but missing from the doc-mirror) + aws:SecureTransport=false condition

KMS key policy (buildDocumentKmsKeyPolicy): CRITICAL + HIGH security-review fixes — both RootAccountFullControl and AppRoleEncryptDecrypt now use Principal field (AWS-canonical) NOT Condition keys. Root break-glass: Principal: arn:aws:iam::<account>:root (was kms:CallerAccount Condition which grants any identity in the account, not just root). App role: Principal: <roleArn> (was aws:PrincipalArn Condition which does NOT reliably match role sessions assumed from the role — silent non-functional grant risk)

17 hermetic tests: Version pin, per-Sid resource scoping, action allowlist checks, explicit assertion that no Allow grants s3:*, no Allow grants iam:*, no Allow uses Resource:* outside ListAllMyBuckets, Principal-based KMS grants (no Condition), DenyLoggingBucketMutation scoped correctly, narrowed IAM deny omits blanket iam:*

docs/IAM-POLICIES.md documents principles, role/policy mapping, bucket-policy + KMS-key-policy rationale, deploy runbook (CMK creation, trail creation, role creation, logs bucket provisioning, account-level BPA, multipart lifecycle rule), and carry-forwards (GuardDuty, Macie, Object Lock, session-credential rotation)

features.description: Image-direct embed (og:image / oEmbed photo / share-info Image URL) under share-link policy
steps: Add `kind` claim to raw-fetch-token: `sub-fetch` (inline 120s, viewer-minted, refinement bypass) vs `external-embed` (long-lived externally-pasted URL, NO refinement bypass)
kind is part of the signed payload — flipping the claim breaks the HMAC signature, blocking downgrade attacks
verifyRawFetchToken returns the verified kind; tokens missing or carrying an unknown kind are rejected as malformed
/l/[hash]/raw maps token kind to bypassRefererRefinement: only `sub-fetch` sets it true; `external-embed` falls through to the F9.7 Sec-Fetch-Dest refinement gate
